chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:
I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who comes to the masjid while its people have already performed the prayer: should he begin with the obligatory prayer, or perform supererogatory prayer?

He said: "If it is within a favorable time, then there is no harm in performing supererogatory prayer before the obligatory prayer. But if he fears missing it because of how much of the time has passed, then he should begin with the obligatory prayer, and that is the right of Allah. Then he may perform whatever supererogatory prayer he wishes. The matter is broad: a person may pray at the beginning of the time of the obligatory prayer. But the merit, when a person prays alone, is that he begins with the obligatory prayer when its time enters, so that the virtue of the time belongs to the obligatory prayer. And it is not forbidden for him to perform the nawafil from the beginning of the time until near the end of the time."

key_terms.النَّوَافِلَ: supererogatory prayers performed in addition to the obligatory prayer
key_terms.الْفَرِيضَةِ: the obligatory prayer due upon the person
key_terms.الْفَوْتَ: missing the prayer or its proper time
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدَ: the masjid, the place of prayer being entered
key_terms.حَقُّ اللَّهِ: the right due to Allah, referring here to the obligatory prayer
key_terms.يَتَطَوَّعُ: to perform a voluntary or supererogatory prayer

ai.seo_question: Should a person pray nawafil before the obligatory prayer when entering the masjid during prayer time?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling on whether one should perform supererogatory prayer or the obligatory prayer first upon entering the masjid after others have already prayed. It teaches that the matter is flexible, but if there is concern about the obligatory prayer time passing, or when seeking the greater merit while praying alone, one should begin with the obligatory prayer.
